headline: Guardrails Before Gadgets
thesis: As AI adoption outruns policy, schools and colleges are leaning on governance, data privacy and interoperability to keep pace.
summary: Search coverage was thin today, with few items dated October 21, so this edition leans on recent and evergreen reporting. The through-line is governance catching up to adoption: CoSN data show cybersecurity and privacy topping K-12 AI worries while few districts have prepared identity and data systems; Brookings argues AI helps students only when used narrowly and designed carefully; and higher ed faculty and students remain divided on AI, with only about 10% of respondents saying their institution is handling it very well. Standards work continued as the 1EdTech Technical Congress wrapped up in Milwaukee (Oct 19–21), and Ed-Fi's 2026 Premier Partners and state impact stories underline data interoperability as the plumbing under it all.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 21, 2026 · Caveat: automated search surfaced few items dated today and the source sites could not be fetched directly, so several entries are recent or evergreen rather than same-day.
